newsitem.title: UK: OPEC Sept crude output up at 25.88 mbpd - IEA.
newsitem.headline: OPEC Sept crude output up at 25.88 mbpd - IEA.

text.p: Crude oil production by the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) rose by a modest 80,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 25.88 million bpd in September, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said in its monthly report published on Tuesday.
The Paris-based energy watchdog saw modest increases from most of OPEC's 11 members in September.
But OPEC's second largest producer, Iran, saw its production fall to 3.67 million bpd from 3.75 million bod in August, the IEA said.
OPEC heavyweight Saudi Arabia increased slightly its output to 8.2 million bpd from 8.12 million in August, the agency said.
The IEA said the decline in Iranian output followed three months of increases. It said September's level is still above the average of 3.65 million in the first half of the year.
"Declining onshore capacity is being roughly balanced by increase in offshore capacity with repair of some fields damaged in the Iran-Iraq War and some new field development," the IEA said.
The IEA blamed a "volatile business environment" on a 45,0000 bpd fall in onshore Nigerian production, primarily in the Bonny and Forcados systems.
"It is reported that fluctuations in the government policy in relation to foreign companies is making it difficult to maintain routine maintenance and necessary workover activities," the IEA said.
OPEC set a production ceiling of 25.033 million bpd for the second half of the year at its ministerial meeting in June, including an extra 800,000 bpd for Iraq.
Including natural gas liquids, supply from the 11 OPEC members totalled 28.61 million bpd from 28.52 million in August, the IEA said.
